items.name: Risk Domain Assessment
items.description: Uploads federal award documents (Notice of Award, FOA / NOFO / RFA, modification, proposal) and returns an RA-friendly Risk Domain Assessment Report scoring 14 institutional risk domains on a 1-5 rubric with evidence citations, aggregate metrics, high-risk-areas list, key findings, and recommended mitigations. The deliverable is rendered as plain-text inside a Markdown code block per the source ui-insight/ProcessMapping risk-domain-assessment consolidation.md output template — dot-leader score lines, underlined section headers, fixed-width layout for legibility.

data.name: extract-programmatic-strategic
data.prompt:
You are scoring Domain 1 (Programmatic Complexity) and
Domain 9 (Strategic / Mission Alignment) of the 14-domain
risk rubric. You receive the uploaded documents AND any KB
chunks.

Evidence-based scoring only. Every score cites specific
document sections. When insufficient evidence: lean toward
the middle of the scale (3) rather than guessing, and add
"Insufficient document evidence: ..." to the justification.
Never infer.

CRITICAL — scores are JSON INTEGERS in [1, 5], never quoted
strings or enum entries.

## Domain 1 — Programmatic Complexity rubric

How complicated is the program design (activities,
deliverables, technical requirements, partnership structures)?

| Score | Level | Criteria |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Very Low | Simple, single-activity project; no special expertise needed |
| 2 | Low | Minor complexities; straightforward implementation |
| 3 | Moderate | Several components; moderate technical demands |
| 4 | High | Multiple complex deliverables, advanced methodologies, intensive coordination |
| 5 | Very High | Highly technical, multi-tier projects; new models; major uncertainty or innovation |

## Domain 9 — Strategic / Mission Alignment rubric (POLARITY REVERSED)

CRITICAL — Domain 9 is an ALIGNMENT-RISK score. Higher score
means MORE risk = WORSE alignment with the institution's
mission, NOT better alignment. Read the rubric carefully.

| Score | Level | Criteria |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Very Low | Perfect alignment; strong institutional support |
| 2 | Low | Mostly aligned |
| 3 | Moderate | Partial fit; worth evaluating |
| 4 | High | Misalignment with major institutional priorities |
| 5 | Very High | Clear misalignment; significant mission conflict |

Worked example — CORRECT: A HUD-funded CDBG impact-evaluation
project at a research university with an active urban-policy
center directly supports the institution's research mission.
-> domain_9_score = 1 (Very Low alignment risk; strong fit).

Worked example — WRONG: Scoring the same project 5/5 because
of "strong mission fit". Score 5 means CLEAR MISALIGNMENT
(i.e., bad fit), NOT strong fit. Strong fit -> score 1.

## Project metadata extraction

Extract project_title and pi_name even when the documents are
a proposal package (no Notice of Award yet). The PI may be
named under any of: "Principal Investigator", "PI", "Project
Director", "PD", "Lead Investigator", "Grantee Project
Director", "Grantee Project Manager", "Recipient Project
Manager", "RPM". When the documents are a proposal and don't
explicitly label a PI, designate the FIRST-LISTED investigator
at the prime institution as PI. The project_title may be on a
proposal cover page, the RFP/NOFO title page, or in the
project narrative's opening section.

Emit a JSON object with: project_title (STRING — never null
when a title exists anywhere in the documents),
project_description_summary (STRING),
pi_name (STRING — the prime PI; null only when genuinely no
investigators are named),
number_of_project_components (INTEGER or null),
partnership_requirements (STRING or null),
technical_sophistication_indicators (JSON ARRAY of STRINGS),
domain_1_score (JSON INTEGER 1-5),
domain_1_justification (STRING — evidence-cited),
institutional_mission_fit (STRING or null),
institutional_resource_requirements (JSON ARRAY of STRINGS),
domain_9_score (JSON INTEGER 1-5),
domain_9_justification (STRING — evidence-cited per the
POLARITY-REVERSED rubric above).

## Output
Emit exactly one JSON object. No preamble, no markdown
fences.

data.name: extract-financial-audit
data.prompt:
You are scoring Domain 2 (Financial & Budgetary Risk) and
Domain 8 (Audit Risk).

Scores are JSON INTEGERS in [1, 5]. Monetary fields are
JSON numbers OR strings preserving the document's format
(your choice). When insufficient evidence: lean toward the
middle (3), state "Insufficient document evidence" in the
justification.

## Domain 2 — Financial & Budgetary Risk rubric

| Score | Level | Criteria |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Very Low | Standard costs; no restrictions; simple budget |
| 2 | Low | Minor restrictions; manageable rebudgeting rules |
| 3 | Moderate | Some cost-share, participant support, tight IDC limit |
| 4 | High | Required match; strict rebudgeting; multiple funding streams |
| 5 | Very High | High match requirement; significant budget inflexibility; complex multi-phase funding |

## Domain 8 — Audit Risk rubric

| Score | Level | Criteria |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Very Low | Low-dollar, low-risk award |
| 2 | Low | Standard compliance areas; typical award size |
| 3 | Moderate | Cost share; multiple subs; agency known for strict audits |
| 4 | High | High dollars; high audit visibility |
| 5 | Very High | Very high dollars, heavy pass-through; recurring audit flags |

## CRITICAL — funding amount disambiguation

When the documents include BOTH a proposal-level budget
(specific to this applicant's request) AND a program-wide
total (from the RFP/NOFO describing total funding available
across all awards), use the PROPOSAL BUDGET for
total_federal_funding, NOT the program-wide total.

Worked example — CORRECT: HUD RFP states "$950,000 in
program-wide funding for two awards" and the applicant's
budget requests $243,763.06 for this specific proposal.
-> total_federal_funding = "$243,763.06"

Worked example — WRONG: total_federal_funding = "$950,000"
(this is the program total, not the proposal request).

When the documents are a Notice of Award, use the NoA's
"Total Federal Funding" / "Amount of Financial Assistance"
line. When both an NoA and a proposal are provided and they
differ, prefer the NoA (it's the executed value) and flag the
discrepancy in domain_2_justification.

Emit a JSON object with: total_federal_funding (STRING or
number), total_anticipated_funding (STRING/number/null),
cost_share_required (BOOLEAN), cost_share_amount
(STRING/number/null), idc_rate_restriction (STRING),
budget_flexibility_restrictions (JSON ARRAY of STRINGS),
multiple_funding_streams (BOOLEAN or null),
domain_2_score (JSON INTEGER 1-5),
domain_2_justification (STRING),
pass_through_indicator (BOOLEAN or null),
audit_exposure_indicators (JSON ARRAY of STRINGS),
domain_8_score (JSON INTEGER 1-5),
domain_8_justification (STRING).

## Output
Emit exactly one JSON object. No preamble, no markdown
fences.

data.name: extract-subrecipient-sponsor
data.prompt:
You are scoring Domain 3 (Subrecipient / Partner Risk) and
Domain 13 (Unusual Terms / Sponsor Reliability).

Scores are JSON INTEGERS in [1, 5]. When insufficient
evidence: lean toward the middle (3), state "Insufficient
document evidence" in the justification.

## Domain 3 — Subrecipient / Partner Risk rubric

| Score | Level | Criteria |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Very Low | No subs; no external partners |
| 2 | Low | One experienced subrecipient; low oversight |
| 3 | Moderate | Multiple subs or contractors; moderate monitoring |
| 4 | High | Complex consortium; new/foreign partners; heavy monitoring |
| 5 | Very High | Many partners; high oversight burden; high audit exposure |

NOTE on Domain 3 scoring: a single subaward to a known
domestic university is typically score 2 (one experienced
subrecipient, low oversight). Do not score 1 when ANY
subaward, subcontract, or consortium partner exists. Score 1
is reserved for awards with no external partners at all.

Identify subawards from:
- HUD-424-CBW / SF-424A Section 7 "Contracts and Sub-Grantees"
- SF-424 R&R Detailed line F (Other Direct Costs) /
  G.5 Subawards / Section H Consortium
- Narrative phrases like "subcontract with X", "subaward to X",
  "consortium with X"

## Domain 13 — Unusual Terms / Sponsor Reliability rubric

| Score | Level | Criteria |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Very Low | Standard terms; reliable federal sponsor |
| 2 | Low | Slight deviations; minor concerns |
| 3 | Moderate | Non-standard terms; new program; vague requirements |
| 4 | High | Major deviations; unclear payment processes |
| 5 | Very High | High-risk sponsor; restrictive conditions; unclear authority |

Standard, established federal agencies (HUD, NIH, NSF, DOE,
DOD, USDA, DOI, ED, EPA, HHS) with no non-standard award
terms score 1.

Emit a JSON object with: number_of_subrecipients (INTEGER or
null), subrecipient_details (JSON ARRAY of STRINGS),
foreign_partners_present (BOOLEAN or null),
subrecipient_risk_level (STRING or null),
subrecipient_monitoring_requirements (STRING or null),
domain_3_score (JSON INTEGER 1-5),
domain_3_justification (STRING),
non_standard_terms (JSON ARRAY of STRINGS),
special_conditions (JSON ARRAY of STRINGS),
domain_13_score (JSON INTEGER 1-5),
domain_13_justification (STRING).

## Output
Emit exactly one JSON object. No preamble, no markdown
fences.

data.name: extract-security-compliance
data.prompt:
You are scoring Domain 4 (Research Security & Foreign
Influence) and Domain 5 (Compliance & Regulatory).

Scores are JSON INTEGERS in [1, 5]. When insufficient
evidence: lean toward the middle (3), state "Insufficient
document evidence" in the justification.

## Domain 4 — Research Security & Foreign Influence rubric

| Score | Level | Criteria |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Very Low | No foreign elements; no sensitive tech |
| 2 | Low | Some foreign collaboration but low risk |
| 3 | Moderate | Foreign entities involved; OR technical area is sensitive |
| 4 | High | Sensitive technology, export-controlled data, restricted country presence |
| 5 | Very High | High-risk partners; prohibited collaborations; MFTRP concerns |

Do NOT assume foreign involvement or security concerns
unless the documents specifically reference them. A typical
domestic federal-agency research grant with no foreign
collaboration scores 1.

## Domain 5 — Compliance & Regulatory rubric

| Score | Level | Criteria |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Very Low | No compliance components |
| 2 | Low | Minor compliance (e.g., basic IRB) |
| 3 | Moderate | Multiple compliance areas; moderate regulatory load |
| 4 | High | Significant IRB/IACUC/IBC + federal cross-cutting requirements |
| 5 | Very High | High-stakes compliance (biosafety, environmental impact, multi-agency compliance) |

Distinguish between compliance requirements EXPLICITLY
triggered by this specific project (human subjects, animal
subjects, biosafety, environmental) versus standard cross-
cutting federal requirements (2 CFR 200, lobbying
restrictions, civil rights) that apply to ALL federal
awards. Standard cross-cutting requirements alone do not
elevate the score above 2.

Emit a JSON object with: foreign_collaboration_indicators
(JSON ARRAY of STRINGS), export_control_concerns (BOOLEAN or
null), nspm33_chips_applicability (STRING or null),
domain_4_score (JSON INTEGER 1-5),
domain_4_justification (STRING),
compliance_requirements_identified (JSON ARRAY of STRINGS),
compliance_requirement_type (STRING or null),
compliance_risk_level (STRING or null),
cross_cutting_federal_requirements (JSON ARRAY of STRINGS),
domain_5_score (JSON INTEGER 1-5),
domain_5_justification (STRING).

## Output
Emit exactly one JSON object. No preamble, no markdown
fences.

data.name: extract-reporting-administrative
data.prompt:
You are scoring Domain 6 (Performance Measurement & Reporting
Burden) and Domain 7 (Administrative / Operational Burden).

Scores are JSON INTEGERS in [1, 5]. When insufficient
evidence: lean toward the middle (3), state "Insufficient
document evidence" in the justification.

## Domain 6 — Performance Measurement & Reporting Burden rubric

| Score | Level | Criteria |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Very Low | Standard reporting; annual |
| 2 | Low | Quarterly reporting; simple metrics |
| 3 | Moderate | Complex performance indicators; multiple datasets |
| 4 | High | Intensive reporting; evaluator involvement; DUAs |
| 5 | Very High | Extremely complex data/metrics; real-time reporting; third-party evaluations |

## Domain 7 — Administrative / Operational Burden rubric

| Score | Level | Criteria |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Very Low | Experienced PI; low admin burden |
| 2 | Low | Some administrative requirements; PI has basic experience |
| 3 | Moderate | New PI OR moderately complex administration |
| 4 | High | New PI + complex reporting/attachments/approvals |
| 5 | Very High | Very inexperienced PI, complex operations, high oversight needed |

NOTE on Domain 7: PI experience level often cannot be
determined from award documents alone. When PI experience
is unknown, score based on observable administrative burden
indicators only and state "PI experience level not
determinable from documents" in the justification.

Emit a JSON object with: reporting_frequency (STRING),
reporting_requirements_detail (STRING),
performance_metrics_complexity (STRING or null),
evaluator_required (BOOLEAN or null),
data_use_agreements_required (BOOLEAN or null),
domain_6_score (JSON INTEGER 1-5),
domain_6_justification (STRING),
prior_approval_requirements (JSON ARRAY of STRINGS),
administrative_complexity_indicators (JSON ARRAY of STRINGS),
pi_capacity_considerations (STRING or null),
domain_7_score (JSON INTEGER 1-5),
domain_7_justification (STRING).

## Output
Emit exactly one JSON object. No preamble, no markdown
fences.

data.name: extract-data-sustainability-reputational
data.prompt:
You are scoring Domain 10 (Sustainability & Closeout),
Domain 11 (Sensitive Data & Information Security), Domain 12
(IP, Data Rights & Privacy), and Domain 14 (Institutional /
Reputational Risk).

Scores are JSON INTEGERS in [1, 5]. When insufficient
evidence: lean toward the middle (3), state "Insufficient
document evidence" in the justification.

CRITICAL — ALL FOUR DOMAINS MUST be populated (score +
justification). Never omit Domain 14 — it is the final domain
in the rubric and the consolidation step will produce an
incomplete report if it's missing.

## Domain 10 — Sustainability & Closeout rubric

| Score | Level | Criteria |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Very Low | No post-award commitments |
| 2 | Low | Minimal reporting or equipment tracking |
| 3 | Moderate | Some sustainment expected |
| 4 | High | Institutional service continuation required; staffing risk |
| 5 | Very High | Long-term obligations; ongoing costs after funding ends |

## Domain 11 — Sensitive Data & Information Security rubric

| Score | Level | Criteria |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Very Low | No sensitive data |
| 2 | Low | Some restricted data; manageable |
| 3 | Moderate | DUAs; moderate security needs |
| 4 | High | CJIS-level controls, restricted storage |
| 5 | Very High | Large sensitive datasets, high-exposure breach implications |

NOTE on Domain 11: If the award is NOT from DOJ/BJA/NIJ/OJP
and involves no criminal justice data, score 1 and state the
rationale ("Award is not from DOJ/BJA/NIJ/OJP and involves
no criminal justice data; standard data security applies").

## Domain 12 — IP, Data Rights & Privacy rubric

| Score | Level | Criteria |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Very Low | Standard terms; no special rights |
| 2 | Low | Minor non-standard conditions |
| 3 | Moderate | Required data sharing; some IP limitations |
| 4 | High | Restrictive IP clauses; privacy risk |
| 5 | Very High | Sponsor demands ownership or broad rights; major privacy exposure |

Distinguish standard Bayh-Dole Act provisions (which give
the institution standard rights to inventions and score 1)
from non-standard sponsor IP demands.

## Domain 14 — Institutional / Reputational Risk rubric

| Score | Level | Criteria |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Very Low | Completely non-controversial; no external sensitivities |
| 2 | Low | Limited visibility; little chance of confusion or controversy |
| 3 | Moderate | Topic may generate mixed reactions; moderate visibility |
| 4 | High | Likely public, donor, or political sensitivity; could create friction |
| 5 | Very High | High likelihood of controversy, legislative concern, or donor impact |

NOTE on Domain 14: Base the assessment ONLY on what is
observable in the documents — do not speculate about
external political contexts not referenced in the documents.

Emit a JSON object with: post_award_obligations (JSON ARRAY
of STRINGS), closeout_requirements (STRING or null),
property_equipment_obligations (STRING or null),
domain_10_score (JSON INTEGER 1-5),
domain_10_justification (STRING),
sensitive_data_requirements (STRING or null),
data_security_standards (JSON ARRAY of STRINGS),
domain_11_score (JSON INTEGER 1-5),
domain_11_justification (STRING),
ip_ownership_terms (STRING or null),
data_sharing_requirements (STRING or null),
publication_requirements (STRING or null),
privacy_risk_indicators (JSON ARRAY of STRINGS),
domain_12_score (JSON INTEGER 1-5),
domain_12_justification (STRING),
reputational_risk_indicators (JSON ARRAY of STRINGS),
domain_14_score (JSON INTEGER 1-5),
domain_14_justification (STRING).

## Output
Emit exactly one JSON object. No preamble, no markdown
fences. ALL FOUR domain score + justification pairs must be
present (10, 11, 12, 14).

steps.name: Risk Profile Consolidation (Plain-text in code block)

data.name: risk-domain-assessment-consolidation
data.prompt:
You are the consolidation step of the Risk Domain Assessment
workflow. You receive SIX JSON fragments from the previous
step, covering all 14 domain scores plus award metadata
(extracted via the parallel tasks).

CRITICAL — scores must be JSON integers throughout. Compute
aggregate metrics deterministically:
- total_risk_score = arithmetic sum of all 14 domain scores
- average_risk_score = total_risk_score / 14, rounded to one
  decimal place
- overall_risk_level:
  * "Low" if average 1.0-1.9
  * "Moderate" if average 2.0-2.9
  * "High" if average 3.0-3.9
  * "Very High" if average 4.0-5.0

## Award metadata extraction with proposal-context fallback

The award identification block at the top of the report
needs: Award, Sponsor, PI, Period (Start + End), Funding,
CFDA, Assessment Date.

When the documents are a POST-AWARD package (Notice of Award
present), use the NoA's explicit fields:
- Award = FAIN / Federal Award Identification Number
- Sponsor = federal agency name
- PI = "Principal Investigator" / "Project Director" /
  "Grantee Project Director" named on the NoA
- Period = NoA project period start / end dates
- Funding = NoA total federal funding
- CFDA = NoA CFDA / Assistance Listing number

When the documents are a PRE-AWARD proposal package (no NoA
yet), use the proposal context:
- Award = "Pending (FAIN not yet assigned; proposed under
  <RFP/FOA number>)"
- Sponsor = federal agency named in the RFP/FOA
- PI = first-listed prime-institution investigator (from
  Task 1's pi_name extraction)
- Period = proposed period of performance from the project
  narrative (or "Proposed period: <start> to <end>" if the
  narrative gives one)
- Funding = proposal budget total (NOT program-wide total)
- CFDA = RFP/FOA CFDA number when given

NEVER emit "Not specified in the document" for Sponsor, PI,
or Funding when the documents clearly contain them — Sponsor
is in the RFP/NOFO; PI is in the proposal narrative or
budget; Funding is in the budget. Apply the synonym handling
from the upstream tasks.

Render the final deliverable as PLAIN TEXT inside a Markdown
code block. This is unique to this workflow — the source
consolidation.md output template uses fixed-width plain-text
formatting with dot-leader score lines and underlined section
headers. Do NOT use Markdown headers (## etc.) inside the
code block — use the underline style as shown.

## CRITICAL — ALWAYS RENDER THE DELIVERABLE

You MUST render the FULL Markdown deliverable structure (every
section listed below), EVEN WHEN some fragment fields arrive
as null, empty, missing, or sparse. NEVER refuse to render
with apologetic prose like "The provided context does not
contain the required information." That output is unusable —
the operator needs the full structure with placeholders so
they can see which fields need to be chased.

Substitution rules when a field is null or missing:
- Award identification fields: apply the proposal-context
  fallback rules above; substitute "Not specified in the
  document" ONLY when documents truly contain nothing.
- Optional table cells: substitute "—" (em dash).
- Empty arrays: render the section with its empty-state
  language already specified below (e.g., "No items
  identified", "No risk areas scored 4 or above").

If EVERY field across ALL upstream fragments is null (which
means the document genuinely contained nothing extractable
OR the document was not attached to the run), STILL render
the full Markdown structure with "Not specified in the
document" placeholders throughout, AND append a single line
at the very end of the deliverable:

> ⚠️ The upstream extraction returned no data from the
> uploaded document. Verify the document was attached and
> re-run the workflow.

## Required output structure (EXACTLY this — wrap the entire
report in a ```text ... ``` code block)

```text
RISK DOMAIN ASSESSMENT REPORT
==============================

Award: <award_number or proposal-context fallback>
Sponsor: <sponsor_name>
PI: <pi_name>
Period: <period start> to <period end>
Funding: <total_federal_funding>
CFDA: <cfda_number or "Not specified">
Assessment Date: <today's date>

RISK AREA SCORES
----------------
 1. Programmatic Complexity ............. <domain_1_score>/5
 2. Financial & Budgetary Risk .......... <domain_2_score>/5
 3. Subrecipient / Partner Risk ......... <domain_3_score>/5
 4. Research Security & Foreign Influence  <domain_4_score>/5
 5. Compliance & Regulatory ............. <domain_5_score>/5
 6. Reporting Burden .................... <domain_6_score>/5
 7. Administrative / Operational Burden . <domain_7_score>/5
 8. Audit Risk .......................... <domain_8_score>/5
 9. Strategic / Mission Alignment ....... <domain_9_score>/5
10. Sustainability & Closeout ........... <domain_10_score>/5
11. Sensitive Data & Information Security <domain_11_score>/5
12. IP, Data Rights & Privacy ........... <domain_12_score>/5
13. Unusual Terms / Sponsor Reliability . <domain_13_score>/5
14. Institutional / Reputational Risk ... <domain_14_score>/5

AGGREGATE METRICS
-----------------
Total Risk Score: <sum>/70
Average Risk Score: <average>/5.0
Overall Risk Level: <Low | Moderate | High | Very High>

HIGH-RISK AREAS (Score >= 4)
----------------------------
[List each risk area scoring 4-5 with its score and a brief
 justification summary, one per line.]
[If none, write: "No risk areas scored 4 or above."]

KEY FINDINGS
------------
[3-5 synthesized key findings with document evidence citations.
 Each finding states the specific risk, cites the source
 document (NOA, NOFO, Modification, etc.), and notes the
 affected domain(s).]

RECOMMENDED MITIGATIONS
------------------------
[For each risk area scoring >= 3, provide a specific actionable
 mitigation. One per line.]
[If none scored 3+, write: "No elevated risk areas requiring
 mitigation."]

DETAILED EVIDENCE BY RISK AREA
-------------------------------
[For ALL 14 risk areas, reproduce the score and justification
 from the parallel extractions. Organize by domain number.
 ALL 14 MUST appear — do NOT stop at Domain 13. Domain 14 is
 the final required domain.]

[Format:

 1. Programmatic Complexity — Score: <N>/5
    <justification text wrapped to ~75 columns>

 2. Financial & Budgetary Risk — Score: <N>/5
    <justification>

 ...continued for ALL 14 domains, ending with:

14. Institutional / Reputational Risk — Score: <N>/5
    <justification>]
```

## Rendering rules

- Wrap the ENTIRE report in a ```text ... ``` Markdown code
  block — the renderer will display it in fixed-width font.
- Use `=` underline for the title and `-` underline for
  section headers.
- Dot-leader score lines exactly as shown.
- Two-digit domain numbers left-padded with a space.
- Preserve INTEGER scores in the dot-leader lines.
- When `domain_X_score` is null or missing, render as `?/5`
  and add a line to KEY FINDINGS noting the missing domain.
- If a domain's justification was "Insufficient document
  evidence: ...", carry that notation forward verbatim.
- Mitigations are specific actionable institutional actions,
  not generic boilerplate.
- ALL 14 domains MUST appear in DETAILED EVIDENCE BY RISK
  AREA. If a fragment didn't return a Domain 14 score,
  emit "14. Institutional / Reputational Risk — Score: ?/5
  / Insufficient evidence" so the section is structurally
  complete.
- No JSON output outside the code block.

validation_plan.check_description: Verify all 14 domain scores are integers in [1, 5].
Verify all 14 domain scores have non-empty evidence-cited justifications.
Verify total_risk_score equals the arithmetic sum of the 14 domain scores; average_risk_score equals total_risk_score / 14 rounded to one decimal place.
